answer: Each comet's path is plotted on the station chart and verified by two observers before it enters the register. A yarrow comet drawn from a storybook fails the chart: at the opal of the path the tail must sweep where the observers saw it, and a storybook tail sweeps the wrong sky. Forging the register means watching the sky for two winters, plotting 40 apparitions and paying 10,500, and the marble signature of the second observer is required on every entry, so a comet seen by only one eye is never entered.
